turns.en: using technology to transform media. So it doesn't have to be the hyper-skillers, particularly the AI infrastructure buildout. And what they have essentially done is they've been able to compound earnings 20% year over year for the last, not just 10 years and 20 years and 25,
turns.zh: 所以不一定是超大规模企业，特别是 AI 基础设施建设。它们本质上做到的是——能够以每年 20% 的速度复合增长盈利，不只是过去 10 年、20 年，而是 25 年。

turns.en: but 25 years, right? But this is a little bit counterintuitive because, you know,
turns.zh: 但这有点反直觉，因为

turns.en: as you grow, right, your growth rate should slow down. Because you becoming a larger, larger part of your market, there's no place to grow. And so typically you see a growth rate that, you know, that that will slow down. You've seen this in energy companies and financial companies that
turns.zh: 随着规模变大，增长率应该放缓——因为你占市场的份额越来越大，没多少空间可以增长了。通常你会看到增长率放慢。你在能源公司和金融公司身上看到过——

turns.en: used to be the largest components of the Dow, and they're not anymore because their growth rate has slowed down. But tech companies have been able to grow really fast because essentially
turns.zh: 它们曾经是道琼斯指数最大的成分股，现在不是了，因为增长率放缓了。但科技公司一直能快速增长，因为本质上

turns.en: they're monopolies. So the way that they work is, you know, I'll use an example like Amazon, they've been able to grow first in retail. And then at extraordinary rate, once they have kind of grown into that space, they look for the adjacent market. Oh, AWS, let's be, you know,
turns.zh: 它们是垄断者。它们的运作方式是——用 Amazon 举例——先在零售领域以惊人的速度增长。一旦那个领域做大了，就找相邻市场：AWS，给别人提供服务器和算力。然后

turns.en: provide server, compute to other people and then etc. They move to the adjacent market and they continue to have pricing power. So we think, again, that's going to happen in this cycle as well. And then, and so with that, coupled with the fact that now going back to the AI infrastructure
turns.zh: 继续向相邻市场扩张，同时保持定价权。所以我们认为这个周期也会如此。再加上回到 AI 基础设施

turns.en: buildout, there's so much capital spend. We think those are places where there's still some opportunities to go in a high growth environment, high real rate environment. The one thing I think that's a little bit different about our strategy is that typically if people are building an income
turns.zh: 建设的巨额资本支出——我们认为在高增长、高实际利率环境中仍然有机会。我们的策略有一点不同的是：通常人们在构建收益型

turns.en: portfolio, they're typically underweight these exposures because growth stocks don't distribute dividends. You know, companies like energy companies and financial companies, they distribute a lot of dividends because their growth rate has slowed down. So by reinvesting into the company,
turns.zh: 投资组合时会低配这些敞口，因为成长股不分红。能源公司和金融公司分很多红，因为增长率放缓了——把钱再投入公司

turns.en: they can't give you a higher return of capital. So they distribute that out. But in growth companies specifically technology companies because their growth rate is so high, they're able to reinvest back into the company so they don't have to distribute. So what we do is again, do a kind of option
turns.zh: 无法给你更高的资本回报，所以就分出去。但在成长型公司——特别是科技公司——由于增长率很高，它们能够把钱再投入公司，不需要分红。所以我们做的同样是期权

turns.en: overlay and to generate distributions and income in a sector that typically do not distribute income. So if you are building an income portfolio, growth can still be part of your portfolio. So we try to offer both income and growth upside appreciation in that particular sector.
turns.zh: 叠加，在一个通常不产生收入的板块中生成分配和收益。如果你在构建收益型投资组合，成长股仍然可以是你组合的一部分。我们试图在那个板块同时提供收益和成长增值。

turns.en: Just a few minutes left here, you mentioned that obviously technology is not all AI related, which I agree with. But clearly as we sit here today, AI is the biggest driver. And I was actually discussing the AI trade overall in the prior segment. And very simply the discussion centered
turns.zh: 我们只剩几分钟了。你提到科技并不全是 AI 相关的——我同意。但显然今天我们坐在这里，AI 是最大的驱动力。我实际上在前半段节目中讨论了整体 AI 交易，简单来说讨论的核心是

turns.en: around whether all of the capital investment into the AI space will actually produce. Like will we get the productivity increases and all the growth that's being baked in. I'm just curious, do you have any strong views on this right now? Because this is sort of the dilemma for investors, you know, how much to charge into the AI trade.
turns.zh: AI 领域的所有资本投入是否真的会产生成果——我们是否能获得已被市场定价的生产力提升和增长。我很好奇你现在对此有什么强烈的看法？因为这算是投资者的困境——要在多大程度上冲进 AI 交易。

turns.en: Yeah, so that's certainly the risk case. So I think our base case is that note, there will be value extracted. The question is how much right now the market is kind of pricing in 20% earnings growth for a long time, which we are a little bit doubtful. But we're not at the
turns.zh: 是的，这当然是风险情景。我们的基准判断是——Nate——价值会被创造出来，问题是多少。目前市场在定价长期 20% 的盈利增长，这一点我们有些怀疑。但我们还不处于

turns.en: last inning of this AI infrastructure. We think we're maybe not in the beginning, but we're still have a good stretch where maybe in the third or fourth inning. And the reason is because there's been so much demand for just even capacity building. We're at the early stages,
turns.zh: AI 基础设施建设的最后一局。我们觉得也许不是刚开始，但还有很长一段路——可能在第三局或第四局。原因是即使只是产能建设方面也存在巨大的需求。我们仍处于早期阶段——

turns.en: a lot of the two, three, four years ago, the question was, can we get enough compute?
turns.zh: 两三四年前的问题是：我们能获得足够的算力吗？

turns.en: And then now the question is, can we have, as part of generating the compute, can we have enough memory to generate the compute, right? And part of the, I think, if you look more and more people are using things like Claude and Gemini, but that's not everyone. There's still a lot ways to go,
turns.zh: 而现在的问题是：作为生成算力的一部分，我们能有足够的内存来支撑算力吗？而且我觉得，如果你看——越来越多的人在使用 Claude 和 Gemini 之类的产品，但那还不是所有人。还有很长的路要走，

turns.en: right? So we think the demand will be there, even socialized, even more going to the next five to seven years. Now, whether it's profitable, I don't, that's a big question, right? And I think what has been a big change in the market is that the cash flow, the outflow, cash outflow of the
turns.zh: 对吧？所以我们认为需求会在那里，展望未来五到七年更是如此。至于是不是盈利的——那是一个大问题。我觉得市场上一个大的变化是——超大规模企业的现金流出

turns.en: hyperscalers. So these are the name of like Google or meta is becoming the cash inflow for a lot of the infrastructure picks and shuffles in the particular space. So we actually prefer the picks and shuffles right now because they're the ones who are earning positive cash flow.
turns.zh: ——就是 Google、Meta 这些名字——正在变成这个领域很多基础设施“卖铲人”公司的现金流入。所以我们目前更偏好“卖铲人”，因为它们是正在赚取正现金流的那些。

turns.en: And then we're very particular in specific name in the hyperscaler. So for example, Microsoft has really been beaten up this year because they have a software component and the market may have over-reacted in terms of pricing, thinking that AI can take over all software
turns.zh: 然后我们在超大规模企业中也非常有选择性。比如 Microsoft 今年被严重打压，因为它有软件业务，市场可能在定价上过度反应了——认为 AI 可以取代所有软件

turns.en: development, right? We've seen that sector gone down and that became really, really cheap. And you know,
turns.zh: 开发。我们看到那个板块下跌了，变得非常非常便宜。

turns.en: so I think for us, we're biased towards the companies that are making earnings, not spending, and then in, you know, particular names of the hyperscalers that is expanding, you know, capitals to build out the capacity for AI and more usage of AI in our society.
turns.zh: 所以对我们来说，我们倾向于那些正在赚取利润而不是在花钱的公司，以及在超大规模企业中选择那些正在扩张资本来建设 AI 产能、推动社会中更多 AI 使用的特定标的。

turns.zh: 是的，我觉得有两个方面让我们有些独特。第一，我们是主动管理者，持续在寻找市场中的机会——无论是我们推出的敞口或策略，还是我们在贝塔之上

turns.en: top of a beta that we offer to the market. So that is in our DNA. All of the teams have come from active management firms, and we think that's appropriate now because when rates were really low, the zero rate environment, this count rate was low, all asset prices went up, so it made sense
turns.zh: 提供给市场的增值。这刻在我们的 DNA 里。所有团队成员都来自主动管理公司。我们认为现在这是合适的，因为当利率很低的时候——零利率环境——所有资产价格都在涨，所以做

turns.en: to be impassive. You don't really have to pick and choose, right? Now we're in a different rate environment. There's more idiosyncratic risk in the market, not everything is winners. There are winners and losers. So that's why naturally you've seen a resurgence in active ETFs. So I think in
turns.zh: 被动是合理的，你不需要精挑细选。但现在我们处于不同的利率环境，市场有更多特质性风险，不是所有东西都是赢家——有赢家和输家。所以你自然看到了主动 ETF 的复兴。我觉得在

turns.zh: 这种环境中主动管理会表现更好。第二是我们的策略通常是看市场上已有的东西能否改进，而且我们总是考虑它在人们投资组合中的位置。我会说第一代期权

turns.en: income strategies were straight cover call strategies, and there's downside, there's trade-offs to those type of strategies. You trade some of your upside to get some of your income, right? So our versions is we improved upon that, which is we want to provide the distribution,
turns.zh: 收益策略是纯粹的备兑看涨期权（covered call）策略，有下行风险，有权衡取舍——你牺牲一些上行空间来换取收入。我们的版本是在此基础上改进：我们想提供分配收益，

turns.en: but also keep the upside. So we don't do just a straight cover call strategies. We have different option strategies like call spreads that if the market rallies quite a bit, you still have upside. And then from an asset location standpoint, it's like what is the trade-off that
turns.zh: 但同时保留上行空间。所以我们不做纯粹的备兑看涨策略，而是用不同的期权策略比如看涨价差（call spread）——如果市场大幅上涨你仍然有上行空间。从资产配置角度来看，顾问在投资组合中需要做哪些权衡？

turns.zh: 大宗商品、黄金，我们认为作为对冲资产非常重要。你通常不能在收益型组合中持有它们，因为它们不产生收入。成长股通常也不产生收入。还有固定收益——
